checklist.evidence: Store amounts as integers in minor units, such as cents, with an explicit currency... Round once per invoice line using a documented rule
Double-entry and append-only... Once an invoice is `open`, it can only be corrected with credit notes.
Every charge carries an idempotency key, `payment:{invoice_id}:{attempt_no}`... process idempotently by PSP event ID, and handle out-of-order delivery.
Card collection uses PSP-hosted elements, so card numbers never reach our systems (PCI SAQ-A). Verify signatures
Postgres **row-level security** keyed on a session variable set by middleware. This protects data even if application code has a bug.
use a keyed state store of `(tenant_id, idempotency_key)` with a TTL longer than the maximum late-arrival window... all raw events go to S3 so any period can be replayed
Measure time to the second and make the policy configurable... never mutate; add new versions
assign invoice number (gapless sequence per seller entity, allocated in txn)... keep invoices for the statutory 7–10 years.
Dunning follows a configurable schedule (for example day 0, 3, 5, 7)... sends emails at each step... entitlements stay in a grace period.
Reconciliation job (nightly): match PSP balance transactions against `payments` and ledger entries. Alert on any mismatch.
Product requests never call billing synchronously. If billing goes down, customers can still use the product
Buy | Build ... Build the full core yourself if pricing is a competitive differentiator

traps.evidence: Store amounts as integers in minor units, such as cents, with an explicit currency.
Finalized invoices never change. Corrections go through credit notes.
Verify signatures, store the raw event, process idempotently by PSP event ID, and handle out-of-order delivery.
card numbers never reach our systems (PCI SAQ-A). We store only tokens.
Postgres **row-level security** keyed on a session variable set by middleware.

note: A technically sound, broad billing architecture with strong money, ledger, idempotency and isolation foundations, but weaker on validation criteria, operations, cost grounding and proportionality.
